title: Compatible smooth charts and normalized diagonal-DNC pasting
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum [def-pur-conventions]: $p$ prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use pro-etale derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For $h=f,g,gf$, put $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$, $W_h=\operatorname{dom}(h)\times_{\operatorname{cod}(h)}\operatorname{dom}(h)$ with first projection $p_h$ and diagonal $\Delta_h$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ [def-pur-section-invariant]. Let $N_h$ be the diagonal normal bundle [def-pur-normal-bundle], with projection $\pi_h$ and zero section $0_h$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Let $\alpha_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ be diagonal base change [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\delta_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_h,0_h)$ normalized DNC [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], formed for the restrictions of $h$ to the affine charts below, where all schemes involved are separated of finite type over $k$ (no separatedness of $X,Y,Z$ over $k$ is assumed), and $\beta_h:C(\pi_h,0_h)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(m_h)[2m_h]$ zero-section bundle purity [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity], where $m_f=d,m_g=e,m_{gf}=d+e$ and twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $\vartheta_h:\omega_h\to\Lambda(m_h)[2m_h]$ for the specified diagonal orientation [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]. Let $\sigma_{f,g}=c_{g,f,\Lambda}^{-1}\theta_{f,\omega_g}\mathrm{sym}$ and $\kappa:C_f\otimes^LLf^*C_g\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{gf}$ be exactly the adjunction-defined maps of [lem-pur-diagonal-section-pasting].

There is an open cover of $X$ by affine $U$, with affine opens $V\subseteq Y$, $T\subseteq Z$, $f(U)\subseteq V$, $g(V)\subseteq T$, and etale charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$, $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Their composite $U\to\mathbf A^{d+e}_T$ is etale, with ordered blocks $(x_1,\ldots,x_d,y_1,\ldots,y_e)$. In these frames the relative tangent sequence is the split exact sequence
$$0\to\mathcal O_U^d\to\mathcal O_U^d\oplus\mathcal O_U^e\to\mathcal O_U^e\to0,$$
with the first inclusion and second projection, and $N_{gf}|_U\cong N_f|_U\oplus f^*N_g|_U$. The coordinate differences identify the diagonal sections with standard zero sections. All schemes to which DNC is applied on these charts are separated finite type over $k$.

All subsequent maps are restricted to such a chart, with $f,g$ also denoting the restrictions. Over $B=U$ put $P_r:\mathbf A^r_B\to B$, let $z_r$ be its zero section and $D_r=Lz_r^*\omega_{P_r}$. Put $q:\mathbf A^{d+e}_B\to\mathbf A^e_B$ and let $\nu_{d,e}:D_d\otimes^LD_e\to D_{d+e}$ be zero-section pullback of $\sigma_{q,P_e}$ using its specified base-change comparisons [lem-pur-diagonal-section-pasting]. In the source-coordinate and actual normal-bundle coordinate identifications of [lem-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-normalization], one has
$$\vartheta_h=\beta_h\delta_h\alpha_h^{-1},\qquad\alpha_{gf}\kappa=\sigma_{f,g}(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g),$$
$$\kappa=\nu_{d,e},\quad\delta_f=1_{D_d},\quad Lf^*\delta_g=1_{D_e},\quad\delta_{gf}=1_{D_{d+e}},$$
and hence, in the corresponding normal-coordinate targets,
$$(\dagger)\qquad\delta_{gf}\kappa=\nu_{d,e}(\delta_f\otimes Lf^*\delta_g).$$
These are the specified exceptional-adjunction coordinate identifications, not arbitrary trivializations. The assemblies and all comparisons commute with further open restriction and etale coordinate restriction. They include $d=0$ or $e=0$, with identity rank-zero data.

proof.text: Fix a point $u\in X$. The last assertion of [lem-pur-affine-difference-tower-factorization], applied to the given smooth separated finite-type pair, supplies affine open neighbourhoods $U,V,T$ of $u,f(u),gf(u)$ and the two specified etale charts of ranks $d,e$. Apply this at every point to obtain the required open cover. The lemma explicitly allows nonseparated ambient schemes: only the restricted affine schemes enter its tower. Fix one such chart for the remaining steps. In Lean, install the structure maps a_Z, g a_Z and f g a_Z, apply exists_compatible_charts, and retain its finite-type and pure-dimension restriction assertions. The etaleness of the ordered composite on each resulting affine triple is the assertion already stated with the tangent calculation in composition_compatible_tangent_normal (steps 2 and 4), so that existing assertion is reused without adding a new obligation.

proof.text: Write the charts as $c_f:U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ and $c_g:V\to\mathbf A^e_T$. The map $\mathbf A^d_V\to\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_T}$ is the base change of $c_g$ along $\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_T}\to\mathbf A^e_T$, hence is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Composing with $c_f$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The definition of affine space identifies its target with $\mathbf A^{d+e}_T$, with coordinates $(x_1,\ldots,x_d,f^*y_1,\ldots,f^*y_e)$ in that order. The restricted composite has relative dimension $d+e$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. In the formal proof, compare the Cartesian ordered-block square of [lem-pur-diagonal-section-pasting] with the Cartesian affine-space base-change square. The unique isomorphism of these two pullbacks carries the explicit composite chart to the first chart followed by the affine-space base change of the second chart: both projections agree by their coordinate formulas. Etaleness follows by base change, composition and cancellation against this isomorphism.

source.place: Proof Step 1: compatible etale normal forms, tangent splitting and diagonal/DNC assemblies; returned proof Steps 4–6

proof.text: The pairs used for $f,g,gf$ have affine bases $U,V,U$ and affine total spaces $U\times_VU$, $V\times_TV$, $U\times_TU$: [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies their rings with the corresponding tensor products. They are finite type over $k$: tensor products of finitely generated $k$-algebras are generated by the two finite sets of generators, and the relative tensor products are quotients of these. Affine spaces over these bases are likewise finite type, by their polynomial-ring description. Their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are affine, hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Thus each diagonal DNC comparison is applied between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, exactly as [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] requires; nothing is applied directly to a nonseparated ambient scheme. The diagonal is regular closed by [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion].

source.place: Proof Step 1: compatible etale normal forms, tangent splitting and diagonal/DNC assemblies; returned proof Steps 4–6

proof.text: For an etale affine chart c:U to affine r-space over V, put R=Gamma(V,O), A=Gamma(U,O), and S=R[t_i]. Its ring map S to A sends t_i to the specified coordinate and constants through h. Identify this map with the chart on affine spectra to see that it is etale. The canonical differential comparison [lem-trf-formally-etale-differentials-base-change] identifies Omega(A/R) with A tensor_S Omega(S/R). The base-changed polynomial differential basis [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] is therefore the basis of the differentials of the chosen coordinates. Compose the universal derivation equivalence [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] with evaluation of linear maps on that basis. This proves the coordinate-evaluation bijection for every A-module, without a purity or DNC input. Apply this to x, to y with restricted scalars, and to the etale composite from step 2. Concatenation and restriction of the two coordinate blocks identify the third evaluation map with the pair of tuples in CompatibleTangentSequence. A relative derivation for f defines a derivation for fg with the same underlying function and vanishes on all pulled-back y coordinates; a derivation for fg restricts along f to a derivation for g. The two evaluation injections prove uniqueness. This gives the ordered frames dx_i, dy_j and (dx_i,d(f*y_j)). Restriction to V is the second projection, and a V-derivation embeds as (v,0); the section inserts (0,w). This gives the split tangent assertion, without needing to construct a separate relative tangent scheme in this module. For the actual normal cones, chartNormalCoordinateMap_spec in the normalization node supplies three isomorphisms preserving their projections and augmentation zero sections. The standard ordered block square of [lem-pur-diagonal-section-pasting] is Cartesian. Paste it vertically with the Cartesian square for affine-space base change along f. Transport this square through the three normal-coordinate isomorphisms. Its canonical isomorphism with the pullback is the defined compatibleNormalSplitting, since both projections agree. Cancellation gives its projection equation and the two zero-section equations. The condition for its pullback lift follows from the same affine-space projection equations. All equations include empty blocks.

proof.text:
For $h=f,g,gf$, [lem-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-normalization] supplies the centred open neighbourhood of its diagonal, the Cartesian zero-section square, and the specified source comparison $c_{h,\mathrm{src}}$ with $D_{m_h}$. In particular coordinate differences are used near the diagonal; no assertion that their entire zero locus in the full self-product is the diagonal is needed. The lemma independently supplies the actual normal-cone comparison $c_{h,N}$ and asserts
$$c_{h,N}\delta_hc_{h,\mathrm{src}}^{-1}=1_{D_{m_h}},\qquad \vartheta_h=\beta_h\delta_h\alpha_h^{-1}.$$
For $g$, pull these comparisons to $U$ along $f$; the base-change clause of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] applies since both $V$ and $U$ are separated finite type. By [lem-pur-affine-difference-tower-factorization], with $Q=U\times_TV$, the square of $G_g:V\times_TV\to\mathbf A^e_V$ and $G:Q\to\mathbf A^e_U$ over $f$ is Cartesian and $Gs=z_e$; so the pulled-back pair is $(b:Q\to U,s)$ with coordinate map $G$. The Cartesian identity of [lem-pur-dualizing-sigma-cocycle-locality] (smooth $P_e:\mathbf A^e_V\to V$, lower arrow $f$, etale $G_g$), pulled back along the sections, identifies $Lf^*c_{g,\mathrm{src}}$ followed by zero-section base change $Lf^*D_e^V\cong D_e$ with the $G$-coordinate comparison $Lf^*C_g\cong Ls^*\omega_b\cong D_e$. So the standard invariant on $U$ is $D_e$ in either description. This proves the three claimed identity DNC maps and the diagonal-orientation formula with the specified maps.

proof.text:
Use [lem-pur-diagonal-section-pasting] for the restricted pair. Its $a,b,s,t$ tower is the twofold diagonal tower for these same $f,g$, and its definitions of $\sigma$, $\kappa$, and $\nu_{d,e}$ are exactly those in the statement. It gives
$$\alpha_{gf}\kappa=\sigma_{f,g}(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g),$$
and its final coordinate assertion gives $\kappa=\nu_{d,e}$ through the canonical exceptional-adjunction coordinate comparisons. For $C_f$ and $C_{gf}$ these are the source comparisons of step 5: both are open restriction followed by the counit-normalized etale exceptional comparison for the same coordinate-difference maps $H_f$ and $F$ of [lem-pur-affine-difference-tower-factorization]. For $Lf^*C_g$ the pasting comparison is the $G$-coordinate comparison through $Ls^*\omega_b$, which step 5 identified with the pulled-back source comparison. Thus no arbitrary trivialization is inserted, and the ordered blocks agree with step 4. The Lean assembly uses the strictly smaller centred source-coordinate transport lemma [lem-pur-centred-diagonal-source-pasting], applied to the ChartEquation obtained from diagonalSectionPasting on the identity open restriction. This retains all specified maps and all three arbitrary centred neighbourhoods.

For the actual pro-etale map use the arbitrary-object tensor square [lem-pur-comparison-tensor-pullback]. Naturality of Dnc.pullComparison moves the ordinary nu across site comparison. Naturality of comparisonTensorNatIso from [lem-sf-comparison-open-tensor-coherence] moves the two section base-change maps across its inverse. Composition of the tensor bifunctor combines these maps with the site pullback comparisons, giving precisely compatibleStandardPullback in the two factors. The remaining normalized DNC restriction specializes chartDiagonalDelta_coordinate_identity and maps Iso.refl through inverse image. The open restrictions of the pasting formulas come from [lem-pur-diagonal-section-pasting], and all squares and compositors include empty coordinate blocks.
